World.title: How Trans-Caspian Cable Fits Kazakhstan’s Evolving Connectivity Strategy
World.content:
ASTANA — For decades, Kazakhstan’s connectivity strategy was measured in highways, railways and pipelines. Today, that vision is expanding. As global competition increasingly depends on the movement of data alongside the movement of goods, the country is investing in a new layer of strategic infrastructure — one designed not to carry cargo, but information.

Among the clearest examples of this shift is the Trans-Caspian fiber-optic cable project. The first-ever underwater telecommunications link across the Caspian Sea will connect Aktau and Sumqayit, creating a new digital corridor between Central Asia, the South Caucasus and Europe.

The project reflects a broader vision articulated by President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev, who has increasingly framed Kazakhstan’s connectivity agenda as extending beyond physical transport routes to include cross-border digital infrastructure. In his September 2024 State of the Nation Address, he called for the project to be completed, describing it as essential for “creating a digital infrastructure linked with international corridors and cross-border data flows.”

Several months later, speaking at an informal meeting of the Council of Heads of State of the Organization of Turkic States in Budapest, Tokayev expanded that vision beyond Kazakhstan.

“This project will significantly improve digital communication between our countries and will be a strategic step towards strengthening regional integration. Such initiatives open up opportunities to create a new digital corridor across the Eurasian continent,” he said.

The regional context continues to evolve. As the cable enters its final construction phase, regional leaders are once again gathering, this time in Cholpon-Ata for an informal Consultative Meeting of the Heads of State of Central Asia and Azerbaijan, underscoring how cooperation between the countries increasingly extends across transport, energy and digital connectivity.

Nearly two years after Tokayev first identified the project as a strategic priority, it is entering its most tangible phase. Kazakhstan is now carrying out the final stages of the project, with commercial commissioning expected by the end of 2026. The latest phase has shifted from engineering preparation to offshore construction.

According to the Ministry of Artificial Intelligence and Digital Development’s release from July 31, regulatory, customs and organizational procedures have been completed, including the approval of equipment required for the offshore works, allowing construction to proceed without administrative delays.

Preparatory work in 2025 included desktop and offshore engineering surveys, selection of the optimal route avoiding anchorage zones and military training areas, environmental approvals from the Mangystau Region authorities, and the production and factory testing in China of a specially armored submarine cable equipped with ROPA optical amplifiers.

With the planning phase complete, attention has shifted from engineering design to execution at sea. The cable, previously delivered from China to the port of Kuryk together with three cable baskets weighing a combined 600 tons, was transported to Baku aboard a specialized logistics vessel. It has now been transferred into the cable tank of the cable-laying vessel, which has departed Baku and is laying the line toward Aktau.

The operation is being carried out by a cable-laying vessel with a displacement exceeding 20,000 tons and equipped with dynamic positioning technology to ensure precise installation on the seabed. Around 70 crew members are involved, including technical supervisors and representatives of Kazakhtelecom. The project is being implemented by CaspiLink B.V., the joint venture established by Kazakhtelecom and AzerTelecom.

A dedicated jointing room has also been installed onboard to allow engineers to repair or reconnect the cable if required during installation. Both the Kazakh and Azerbaijani cable ends have already undergone testing. Subject to favorable weather conditions, installation of the submarine cable is expected to be completed within the next 15 to 20 days, while the overall commissioning process remains on schedule for completion by the end of 2026.

The significance of the project, however, extends well beyond the technical operation. As economies become more deeply integrated through both physical and digital infrastructure, international corridors are no longer defined solely by the goods they carry. They are increasingly shaped by the data they enable to move across borders. While the cable spans just 380 kilometers across the Caspian seabed, the vision behind it reaches much further. The Trans-Caspian fiber-optic cable reflects Kazakhstan’s ambition to remain an important link in the movement of both goods and data across Eurasia.

World.title: Russian woman faces prison after calling Armenians ‘rat-like’ people
World.content:
Russian calls Armenians ‘rats’

A criminal case has been opened in Armenia against Russian national Nadezhda Pirozhkova. A blogger who has lived in Armenia for the past year and a half, Pirozhkova came under fire after criticising Vardavar, the Armenian tradition of pouring water over one another on the holiday. She described the custom as an act of aggression. In another video, she referred to Armenians as a “rat-like people”.

Armenia’s Investigative Committee has initiated criminal proceedings against Pirozhkova under the article on “public statements aimed at inciting hatred and discrimination through the use of the internet”. Armenia’s Criminal Code provides for a prison sentence of up to four years under this article. If Pirozhkova is found guilty in court, she could therefore face imprisonment.

For now, however, she has been banned from leaving her place of residence as a preventive measure. The blogger may leave Yerevan only with written permission from a prosecutor or a judge.

Vardavar is one of the principal feasts of the Armenian Apostolic Church, celebrating the Transfiguration of Jesus Christ, although its origins date back to pagan times. It is virtually impossible to stay dry on the streets that day, but taking offence is not customary, as drenching someone with water is considered a way of congratulating them on the holiday. The water is believed to bring health, good fortune and purification.

Pirozhkova’s Instagram posts sparked outrage among social media users—not only Armenians, but also fellow Russians.

Many have not only criticised Pirozhkova but have also called on law enforcement authorities to punish her as severely as possible or deport her from the country.

Political commentator Artyom Yerkanian did not rule out the possibility that certain actors interested in damaging Armenia’s image as a tourist destination were behind the spread of such videos. He pointed to the large number of Russian tourists visiting Armenia. In the first half of 2026 alone, Armenia received 1.042 million foreign visitors, around 40% of whom were from Russia.

“It’s interesting, isn’t it? On the one hand, the Russian government imposes trade restrictions [on imports of Armenian products and goods], while on the other, Russians happily travel to Armenia, enjoying its nature, its people and, why not, its traditions,” Yerkanian said.

What else Pirozhkova said

In a video about Vardavar, the Russian blogger said that the holiday made her want to leave Yerevan more than anything else. She described the tradition of pouring water over one another as “the height of tactlessness”. In her view, Armenians do not understand the concept of “personal boundaries” and routinely violate them.

Pirozhkova argued that splashing passers-by with water was disrespectful towards those who did not wish to take part in the celebration.

“If I’m in your country, I’m not obliged to follow your traditions. This is a direct manifestation of aggression.“

Following the video, Pirozhkova has periodically posted about the wave of online abuse directed at her. She has also publicly apologised several times, saying:

“I understand that many people saw it as disrespect towards the Armenian people. And I’m truly sorry. That was never my intention, and it still isn’t.”

At the same time, the blogger has acknowledged that she is using the controversy to promote her Instagram page.

“People recognise me now. Why shouldn’t I make use of something I’ve been through after putting in so much effort? I’ve worked hard for this. Why shouldn’t a person take advantage of circumstances and situations they have rightfully earned? I just want to change my life.“

Foreign nationals are required to respect Armenia’s national customs and traditions

The legal status of foreign nationals in Armenia is governed by the Law on Foreigners. Article 5 of the law states that foreigners in Armenia enjoy the same rights, freedoms and obligations as Armenian citizens. At the same time, it stipulates that “foreigners in the Republic of Armenia are obliged to respect the Constitution and laws of the Republic of Armenia, other legal acts, as well as national customs and traditions.”

The same article also provides that foreign nationals bear the same legal responsibility as Armenian citizens while in Armenia.

Armenia’s Criminal Code provides for penalties for “public statements aimed at inciting or promoting hatred, discrimination, intolerance or hostility against an individual or group of persons on the grounds of race, nationality or ethnicity, as well as the dissemination of materials or objects for that purpose.”

The available penalties include fines, community service, restriction of liberty and imprisonment.

Under Article 329, offences committed “through publicly displayed works, the mass media, or information and communication technologies” are punishable by one to four years’ imprisonment

Commentary

Political commentator Artyom Yerkanian said in an interview with a local television channel::

“After the Russian blogger publicly apologised, this story could have ended there. But some social media users continued calling on the Armenian law enforcement authorities to examine Nadezhda Pirozhkova’s actions and determine whether they amounted to a criminal offence. The authorities decided to respond to those calls.

Perhaps there was no need to be so severe. The court will, of course, take all mitigating circumstances into account.

Perhaps we should not politicise everything. It is obvious that the aim was not to incite ethnic hatred but simply to increase her audience through provocative videos.

In two weeks, the video attracted more than 250,000 views and over 5,000 comments. As a result, the number of followers on her page increased more than fifteen-fold.

In other words, this blogger simply found a ridiculous and foolish way to grow her audience.

Nevertheless, perhaps such cases should be monitored more closely, because this is not an isolated incident.

In recent weeks, there have been several similar cases in which foreign bloggers, particularly Russians, have made remarks discrediting Armenians and damaging Armenia’s reputation as a tourist destination.

There was one case in which a young woman accused an Armenian taxi driver of attempting to rape her. I also recall another similar incident, and there are probably many more. But what is more important?

Notably, these videos are deliberately amplified by non-existent users. An army of fake accounts is spreading this material in pursuit of a specific objective.

It cannot be ruled out that certain forces are behind these fake accounts and are interested in ensuring that Armenia is not perceived as a safe destination for tourists.

Every tourist who enjoys visiting the country indirectly becomes its ‘agent of influence’. Perhaps that is exactly what some people dislike.

I don’t know whether it is a coincidence, but it was precisely during those days that the Russian Foreign Ministry added Armenia to its list of countries where Russians cannot feel safe, citing the possibility that the Armenian authorities could extradite them to third countries. Perhaps it is a coincidence—or perhaps it is not.”

Social media reaction

“If, after a year and a half of living in Armenia, she still allows herself to speak like this, it cannot be dismissed as an accident or naivety.”

“The police should investigate her actions. She’s a planted agent.”

“She should be fined heavily and deported.”

“She should be tried and deported from our country. It’s a matter of the nation’s dignity.”

“If an Armenian had behaved like this in Russia, he would already have disappeared.”

“Foreign visitors are obliged to obey the law, respect the country and its people, and behave like guests.”

World.title: Meet Nitsa, Elvis and Oliver: Pine martens at Tbilisi Zoo. Video
World.content:
Nitsa, Elvis and Oliver are young pine martens and the newest residents of Tbilisi Zoo. A local resident found the orphaned cubs alone in an attic and took them home after discovering they had no mother.



However, pine martens are wild predators with powerful teeth and strong natural instincts. Once the cubs had grown up, releasing them back into the wild was no longer an option. Contact with humans had altered their natural behaviour, leaving them unable to survive on their own. Their rescuer therefore turned to Tbilisi Zoo for help.

Konstantin Pkhakadze, head of the zoo’s exotic animals department, said the pine martens arrived at Tbilisi Zoo about a month ago. He said such cases are quite common. People often assume that young animals found alone have been orphaned and need rescuing, but that is not always the case.

In most instances, the mother is nearby, hunting, searching for food or moving her young to a new location. Pkhakadze said intervening at that stage is the biggest mistake people can make. They should not even approach the cubs, as the mother may detect the scent of humans, see it as a threat and never return to her offspring.

Tbilisi Zoo currently has very limited capacity to take in new animals. Its existing site is overcrowded, while most of its resources are being directed towards the construction of a new zoo.

Nitsa, Elvis and Oliver were initially housed in the zoo’s exotics pavilion. However, the small enclosed space was unsuitable for such active and energetic animals. Zoo staff therefore built a temporary outdoor enclosure, giving the pine martens more space, fresh air and room to move freely.

Tbilisi Zoo‘s history spans nearly a century. It was founded on 10 February 1927 on the basis of the Caucasian Society for the Acclimatisation of Animals, which had been keeping wild animals since the early 20th century, though without official zoo status. The zoo was originally built on 70 hectares in the Vere River gorge. Over the years, the expansion of the capital — and later the devastating flood of 13 June 2015 — significantly reduced the territory of the old zoo. Today, it covers five hectares and is home to around 1,500 animals, each with its own story. In this video series, we will introduce you to the residents of Tbilisi Zoo. We will show how their day unfolds, how they interact with other animals and people, and how their behaviour changes depending on the weather and the season. Get ready to hear many fascinating stories.

Pine martens at Tbilisi Zoo

World.title: Georgia’s opposition launches campaign to restore voting rights for emigrants
World.content:
In Georgia, the opposition alliance Coalition for Change and the Strategy Aghmashenebeli party have launched the Emigrant’s Vote campaign, calling for the restoration of Georgian citizens’ right to vote from abroad in parliamentary and municipal elections.

Under the new Election Code, approved by the ruling Georgian Dream party on 17 December 2025, emigrants are no longer allowed to vote from abroad. Instead, they must travel to Georgia to cast their ballots.

One of Coalition for Change’s members, Tengo Tevzadze, announced the launch of the campaign, saying the initiative would culminate in a constitutional challenge seeking to restore emigrants’ right to take part in elections.

According to Tevzadze, the campaign aims to demonstrate that allowing emigrants to vote is consistent with Georgia’s constitution and that every Georgian citizen, regardless of where they live, should be able to take part in elections.

Tevzadze noted that Georgian Dream won just 13.4% of the overseas vote in the disputed 2024 parliamentary election, which the opposition says was rigged. He argued that this was why the authorities later moved to strip emigrants of their voting rights.

Tevzadze argues that depriving emigrants of the right to vote violates Georgia’s constitution and is unfair to a group of citizens that makes a significant contribution to the country’s economy.

The campaign’s organisers have set out two main demands: restoring emigrants’ right to vote and creating an electoral system that allows Georgian citizens living abroad to cast their ballots.

“We need as many emigrants as possible to sign the petition so that, alongside political efforts, we can also challenge the regime through legal means. Through a constitutional lawsuit, we will clearly demonstrate that emigrants’ participation in elections and their voting rights are protected by the constitution, and that Georgians, both at home and abroad, must be able to take part in free and fair elections,” Tengo Tevzadze said.

Voting rights for Georgian emigrants

World.title: Evening illuminations in South Ossetia: Video
World.content:
Evening illuminations in South Ossetia

Major reconstruction work has been completed in the South Ossetian capital, Tskhinval. The city centre has been renovated, dozens of streets repaired, and new utility networks installed.

The redevelopment of Theatre Square included new lighting, benches and marble planters, while boxwood and juniper shrubs were planted. Several school and college buildings, along with the Kosta Khetagurov State Drama Theatre, have also been restored.

The work was funded through Russia’s investment programme.

The terminology, place names and views expressed in this article are those of the author and do not necessarily reflect the editorial position of this website.

World.title: Russian mass strike on Ukraine leaves several dead and dozens injured. Video from Lviv
World.content:
Russian strike on Ukraine: Video from Lviv

Russia launched a mass overnight attack on Ukraine on 30 July, according to Ukrainian authorities, firing a total of 74 missiles and 284 attack drones. Ukraine said its air defences intercepted a significant number of the incoming targets, but some missiles and drones struck their intended targets.

Several regions across Ukraine came under attack, including Lviv, Kyiv and the Dnipropetrovsk region.

In Lviv, one resident was killed. In the village of Radushne, near Kryvyi Rih, a ballistic missile struck the home of a large family. Six people were killed, including three children, while several others were injured.

Lviv Mayor Andriy Sadovyi said the city had suffered direct Russian missile strikes on residential buildings for the first time in a long period.

The heaviest damage was reported on Paton and Vyhovskoho streets, where more than 20 residential buildings, a school, two kindergartens and other civilian infrastructure were damaged.

Rescue workers recovered the body of a man from beneath the rubble.

According to the latest official figures, 34 people, including three children, were injured in the attack on Lviv. Nine people were rescued from damaged buildings. Emergency crews are continuing search and rescue operations and clearing the debris.

Lviv city authorities said some residents whose homes were damaged would be provided with temporary accommodation, while municipal services are assisting those left homeless.

Russian strike on Ukraine: Video from Lviv

World.title: German broadcaster ARD investigates Georgia’s rise as a crypto hub
World.content:
Crypto mining in Georgia

“Crypto war: How Putin is using bitcoin to wage war against us” is the title of a 45-minute investigative documentary by German public broadcaster ARD, which portrays Georgia as a major cryptocurrency mining hub and an alleged transit route used by Russia to circumvent Western sanctions.

The documentary focuses on bitcoin mining and crypto systems which, the journalists argue, have enabled Russia to adapt to international financial restrictions.

Georgia’s favourable conditions for crypto industry

The investigation’s authors say Georgia has developed a particularly favourable legal and tax environment for the cryptocurrency industry over many years. They argue that this was closely linked to political and economic decisions taken during the rule of the Georgian Dream party and its founder, Bidzina Ivanishvili, turning the country into what they describe as one of the world’s cryptocurrency “grey zones”.

The documentary focuses in particular on the free industrial zones in Poti and Rustavi. According to the journalists, Russia can no longer sell natural gas to Europe at pre-sanctions levels, with some of that gas instead being used to generate low-cost electricity. The filmmakers argue that this electricity powers large-scale bitcoin mining infrastructure, the ultimate financial benefits of which serve Russia’s interests.

The German journalists say they travelled to Georgia and visited cryptocurrency mining facilities themselves, including infrastructure in the Rustavi Free Industrial Zone.

Russia said using cryptocurrency to circumvent sanctions

Nino Bakradze, founder of the investigative journalism organisation iFact, says in the documentary that Russia has not been completely cut off from the international financial system and is increasingly using cryptocurrency for cross-border transactions.

Nino Bakradze

She says iFact investigated exports of dual-use goods to Russia by conducting an undercover experiment. The organisation contacted a Russian trading company and asked whether it could ship around 30 drones to Russia. According to Bakradze, the company replied that such a shipment was possible and said it had carried out similar transactions before despite the risks posed by sanctions.

Bakradze says the investigation found that companies involved in such transactions use cryptocurrency to settle payments in order to circumvent sanctions, often without being detected by Western authorities.

‘Bitcoin mining in Georgia is profitable’

The documentary also features local bitcoin miner Nikoloz Museridze, who says the main advantage of mining bitcoin in Georgia is the country’s relatively low electricity prices.

Nikoloz Museridze

Museridze says his mining farm consumes about 2 megawatts of electricity. He estimates that, at this capacity, it takes about a year to mine one bitcoin, while the cost of producing a single bitcoin in Georgia is around $30,000-$40,000.

The miner describes bitcoin as “borderless money” that can be transferred anywhere in the world at any time and which, he claims, cannot be blocked or frozen.

World.title: Nauru withdraws recognition of occupied Abkhazia and South Ossetia
World.content:
The government of the Pacific island nation of Nauru says it has formally withdrawn its recognition of the self-proclaimed republics of Abkhazia and South Ossetia as independent states.

“The Government of the Republic of Nauru declares that it has withdrawn its recognition of the ‘Republic of South Ossetia’ and the ‘Republic of Abkhazia’ as independent states.

Accordingly, the Republic of Nauru has immediately terminated diplomatic relations with South Ossetia and Abkhazia,” the Nauru government said in a statement.

On 29 July, Nauru severed diplomatic relations with the Russian-occupied Georgian regions of Abkhazia and South Ossetia.

Georgia’s foreign ministry described the decision as a sign of respect for the principles of international law and said Tbilisi was ready to establish diplomatic relations with Nauru and strengthen bilateral cooperation on the basis of shared interests.

“The decision once again confirms that respect for and adherence to international law are the foundation of healthy international relations,” the ministry said in a statement.

The self-proclaimed Abkhaz foreign ministry claimed that Nauru had come under “unprecedented pressure” to end diplomatic relations with Abkhazia.

“The development of cooperation between the Republic of Abkhazia and the Republic of Nauru has consistently encountered resistance from Georgia and its Western partners. As joint initiatives turned into practice, a campaign of aggressive external pressure was unleashed against the Republic of Nauru.

For many years, states maintaining diplomatic relations with the Republic of Abkhazia have faced external pressure aimed at abandoning their independently determined foreign policy course. Small states, with limited resources to counter large-scale political, diplomatic, and economic instruments of influence, are particularly vulnerable to such pressure.

Such practice contradicts the fundamental principles of the UN Charter, including the principles of the sovereign equality of states and non-interference in their internal affairs.

The Republic of Abkhazia remains committed to strengthening its international subject status, protecting its national interests, and developing mutually beneficial cooperation with states that share the principles of sovereign equality, mutual respect, and international law,” the statement said.

Nauru recognised the independence of Abkhazia and Georgia’s Tskhinvali region (South Ossetia) in 2009, after Russia declared the two Georgian regions independent states. Nauru was one of only a handful of countries to support the move backed by Moscow.

Nauru is a small Pacific island state in the Micronesia region. It is one of the world’s smallest countries, both by land area and population. Covering about 21 sq km (8 sq miles), it is home to around 12,000-13,000 people.

World.title: Pashinyan: ‘Russia wants either exclusive ties or nothing’
World.content:
Pashinyan rejects exclusive ties with Russia

Armenian Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan has once again addressed the current state of relations between Armenia and Russia. He commented in particular on Russia’s restrictions on imports of Armenian goods, an issue that has caused growing concern in Armenia. During a briefing, Pashinyan said the country should view the situation not as a crisis but as an opportunity to diversify its economy.

Journalists asked him to address the political dimension of the issue, arguing that it clearly extends beyond economics. Pashinyan said the problem stems from Armenia’s search for alternatives that it previously did not have.

As an example, he pointed to the signing of strategic partnership agreements with China, the United States, the United Kingdom, the Netherlands, France and other countries.

According to Pashinyan, Armenia had never before had — and could not have had — strategic relations with so many partners.

“I cannot speak about Russia’s feelings. I can say that Russia sees this as a problem. There is also an element of exclusivity here. The issue is this: either the relationship is exclusive, or there should be no relationship at all. We do not share that view,” he said.

Pashinyan said Yerevan’s position is “legitimate.” Armenia’s ties with Russia are not exclusive, he said, but the relationship should continue.

“I ask that our position be treated with understanding and respect, especially since its legitimacy is not questioned in practice,” he said.

Pashinyan also stressed that Armenia would continue discussions with Russia over the economic restrictions that Russia and the Eurasian Economic Union have imposed on Armenian goods.

“That would be the worst possible course of action,” he added.

“What was wrong with Armenia? What did Armenia do?”

Journalists asked why Russia places such importance on Armenia’s political orientation and whether Pashinyan had given Moscow any reason to doubt that Armenia remains a reliable partner. In response, the prime minister posed a series of questions:

“What was wrong with Armenia in 2022 that the Collective Security Treaty Organization failed to fulfil its obligations? What did Armenia do wrong? Whom did Armenia harm? What did Armenia do that justified what happened?” he said, referring to Russia’s and the CSTO’s failure to respond after Azerbaijani forces entered Armenia’s internationally recognised territory in 2021–2022, despite the alliance’s obligation to act in the event of an attack on a member state’s territorial integrity.

What was wrong with Armenia that the Russian peacekeepers in Karabakh failed to fulfil their mission? Was the problem October 2022?” he continued, referring to the 6 October 2022 statement signed by Armenia and Azerbaijan in Prague, in which the two countries recognised each other’s territorial integrity. “But there were incidents even before that. What was wrong with Armenia? And why is it always assumed that we are the bad partner?”

“We are showing who needs Armenia”

Continuing on the issue, Pashinyan referred to Belarusian President Alexander Lukashenko’s remark, “Who needs Armenia?”

“Has Armenia harmed anyone? Has it harmed Belarus? How can anyone speak about a sovereign state like that?” he said.

Pashinyan argued that the Belarusian president had asked the question but failed to find an answer. Now, he said, Armenia is showing exactly who values relations with it.

“Armenia matters to China, the United States, the European Union and Iran. And Armenia needs all of those partners as well. Georgia needs Armenia, and Armenia needs Georgia. Armenia matters to France, Germany, Poland and the United Kingdom. That’s the whole story.”

“The alternative is not yet in place” for a referendum

In recent months, Moscow has repeatedly urged Armenia to choose between the Eurasian Economic Union and the European Union. Russian officials have insisted that Armenia should hold a referendum on the issue as soon as possible. At the end of May, the leaders of four EAEU member states issued a joint statement calling for such a vote.

“I respect the fact that, on 29 May, the leaders of four EAEU countries issued a statement supporting the idea of a referendum on EU membership. But there is still nothing to vote on,” Pashinyan said.

He reiterated that it would make sense to hold a referendum only after Armenia obtains EU candidate status or once the issue formally appears on the agenda.

According to the prime minister, Moscow does not challenge Yerevan’s right to pursue alternatives. Instead, it is telling Armenia: “Decide today which alternative you choose.”

“But the alternative is not yet in place. The process of creating it has only just begun. It would be dishonest to ask people now whether they support an alternative that does not yet exist. They would ask many questions that we simply cannot answer today,” he said.

Pashinyan said the government would continue working to answer those questions before asking the public to make a choice.

Pashinyan rejects exclusive ties with Russia

World.title: Housing market seeing 'rapid deterioration' as property downturn deepens
World.content:
Australia's housing downturn is spreading across the country, with previously resilient property markets that had recently set record-high prices now experiencing a decline in values.

The latest figures from property data firm Cotality show national property prices in July fell 0.7 per cent, making it the largest single monthly decline in value since December 2022.

The data shows the downturn is no longer confined to Sydney and Melbourne, with property prices in Brisbane and Adelaide falling by 0.6 per cent and 0.2 per cent respectively. It is the second-consecutive month of declines for both cities after Cotality revised its data from June.

"There's been a really rapid deterioration in conditions in Brisbane, which I think has probably been the most surprising trend that we've seen over the last couple of months," Cotality's head of research Gerard Burg told The Business.

"The shift is really evident in the total stock available for sale [in Brisbane]. Going back to February, it was around 25 per cent below the five-year average. It's now sitting up around 6 per cent above that average level."

In other words, the amount of available housing supply in Brisbane has accelerated, giving buyers more choice.

Elsewhere, Perth managed a modest 0.1 per cent increase following a revised 0.5 per cent contraction in June, while Darwin recorded an increase of 0.8 per cent.

The weakening housing market is welcome news for first home buyers, with Melbourne real estate agent Shahid Khan starting to see more confident bidders.

"What we have seen lately in the last few weeks — the buyers are there, limited buyers," Mr Khan said.

" There's a bit of hesitancy in the marketplace, especially with the borrowing capacity, but first home buyers are still bidding strong. "

Are falling house prices affecting you? Tell us Share your experiences or stories with us here

Mr Burg said while property values will likely continue deteriorating across the country, he expects more vendors (or sellers of property) to start pulling back from the market as they grow increasingly hesitant to lose money on a sale.

"When vendors look out at the market, they are seeing these challenging conditions and they're probably thinking that they've missed the opportunity to sell at the market peak," he said.

" If they have that choice to wait, they're going to wait for the next cycle once conditions improve to put their home on the market. "

Sellers could start withdrawing from the market to try and secure a higher price in the future. (ABC News: Danielle Bonica)

Are there more declines on the horizon?

Mr Burg said changes to negative gearing and capital gains tax have contributed to the wider softening of the national housing market, as has the three interest rate hikes by the Reserve Bank of Australia this year.

"It is continuing to have an effect because these policy issues can take time for people to really process the change and consider what's happening," Mr Burg said.

"On the rate increases, these moves that we've seen so far have increased the necessary income to make a home purchase, as that borrowing capacity has been pulled back, even in markets where we have seen home values decline over the last couple of months.

"So they're both things that tend to fall over the space of a number of months."

Gerard Burg from Cotality expects property values will continue declining in the short-term. (ABC News: Darryl Torpy)

Former chief economist for NAB, Alan Oster, believes the property market weakness is more connected with rising interest rates.

"I think it's mainly the higher interest rates," Mr Oster said.

The now-independent economist said there was a fear among investors and owner-occupiers that interest rates might climb higher, even though economists broadly expect rates will remain on hold after the RBA's meeting on August 11.

"There's a little bit of uncertainty about whether [the Reserve Bank] might even do more [rate hikes]," he said.

" And then you've got issues about negative gearing which people get nervous about and they worry that that's going to cause the market further problems. But ultimately to me, this is an interest rate effect. "

Coupled with a weakening economy, he warned it could result in the unemployment rate moving well above the current level of 4.4 per cent to see more falls in property prices.

"I think if there was a 5 in front of [the unemployment rate], that's getting very close to a recession," Mr Oster said.

Property prices have declined in Brisbane after recent strong growth. (ABC News: Michael Lloyd)

In this scenario, Mr Oster said, he would expect a property market correction, or a fall in prices from the recent peak of 10 per cent or more.

"You can't say exactly, but I think you'd probably be expecting 10 to 15 per cent fall [in property prices]," he said.

"At the end of the day, if that did happen, the [RBA] would be cutting rates."

Despite the current "swift loss of momentum", Mr Burg argued there are a number of factors currently supporting the market that would prevent such a dramatic fall in property prices.

"Certainly, unemployment still remains very low ... we have continued population growth ... and there are some challenges on the supply side too," he said.

"New construction remains very, very difficult, and particularly as value starts to come off, the feasibility of a lot of these new construction projects becomes a lot harder.

"So you have a situation of, if unemployment remains quite low, we don't have a lot of forced sales, that could limit that degree of supply side pressure to really drive values much lower.

" This could be perhaps a prolonged, but not necessarily enormously deep downturn in values across the country. "

World.title: Diamonds win bronze medal with an eye to greater things for netball
World.content:
There's a sentiment in team sports at multi-sport events like the Commonwealth Games that you lose silver and win bronze.

The bronze medallists get to climb on the podium having won their last match, while second place is coming off a heartbreaking loss, having let gold slip through their grasp.

For the Diamonds, bronze at the 2026 Commonwealth Games is a complicated celebration.

Less than 20 hours after Jamaica ripped their hearts out in the semifinal, the Aussie netballers were back on court at 9am in Glasgow for the first centre pass of their first-ever bronze-medal match.

Diamonds fumble Australia's most anticipated gold medal The Diamonds will miss the Commonwealth Games gold medal match for the first time after a shock semifinal loss to Jamaica in front of a crowd baying for Australia's downfall.

It was hard to bounce back from the loss but they did so against England, winning 65-80.

"We had such a quick time to process what happened, I think a lot of us still feel quite numb," defender Jo Weston said.

"Then you go out and have a game like we did, we're so proud and we know all of Australia have been behind us, so it's been a real rollercoaster of emotions in a very short time frame. But I think the overwhelming feeling is pride and a lot of love for each other.

"It's immensely challenging for us having that mental fortitude to come back out. We have very high expectations of ourselves and we want to do our country proud.

The Diamonds rediscovered their flow to keep their medal-winning streak alive. (AP: Andrew Milligan/PA)

"They always say Diamonds are made under pressure and I think that really showed in us today. Although it's not the colour we were after we're really proud about it."

Coach Stacey Marinkovich said the night between the games was about leaving space for team members to "be vulnerable".

There was no point pretending they weren't gutted, that the loss was anything other than gut-wrenching, but once they left the meeting room it was about moving forward.

"It was very emotional last night, it was still probably lingering today a little bit, so to be able to mentally switch in showed our culture isn't words on a wall," she said.

There were complicated emotions for Australia's bronze medallists. (Getty Images: James Fearn)

"That took a lot of grit to be able to go out there and get that result."

Adding another layer of emotion for these stewards of the game, constantly fighting for eyeballs and recognition, is the more objective flip-side of the loss.

That is those celebrations of the Sunshine Girls after the semifinal.

For the first five Commonwealth Games, only Australia and New Zealand won gold and silver. In 2018, England stunned the Diamonds on their home patch for the Gold Coast title. Four years ago Jamaica beat the Aussies in their group match and made their first final. And in Glasgow, they went even better to take the Diamonds down in a knockout match to fight New Zealand for gold.

"International netball is the best it's ever been, which is so good for the sport, it's what we want to see," Weston said.

Four countries is not an enormous range of winners or even contenders, but in every event around the world there are dominant forces.

It wasn't the colour they wanted or expected, but a medal's a medal. (Getty Images: James Fearn)

With six years to the Brisbane Olympics and a push for the sport's inclusion, the Diamonds' bronze may have been the best thing for game.

"It's great for the sport because we always want the game to grow. Gone are the days where it's just one or two nations really dominating," Kiera Austin said.

"It's disappointing for us to have not gotten to that point ... but Jamaica were far too good on the day and that's great going into Brisbane hopefully getting netball into the Olympics.

"It's a sport we absolutely love, a sport we think deserves a great platform on the international stage and if it means a greater competition, then winning that gold medal whenever we get the chance to again is going to be all that much sweeter."

World.title: Moscow mayor calls deadly bomb attack on a restaurant a 'terrorist act'
World.content:
Moscow mayor Sergei Sobyanin has called a bomb attack on a restaurant in the capital a "brutal terrorist act", but did not say who was responsible.

The blast on Saturday evening at the Balzi Rossi, an upscale Italian establishment in central Moscow, killed three people, including the female bomber, Russian state media said, citing local officials.

"Yesterday, a brutal terrorist act was committed in Moscow that claimed human lives. The victims are currently in the city's hospitals, where they are receiving all necessary care," Mr Sobyanin wrote on social media Sunday.

At least 21 people were wounded when the explosive device detonated at the restaurant on Kudrinskaya Square, Russia's National Anti-Terrorism Committee (NAK) said late on Saturday, according to Russian state news agency Ria Novosti.

The woman attempted to smuggle the bomb into the establishment, but the security guard refused to let her in before the bomb exploded, reported Ria Novosti.

The Moscow Investigative Committee said the attack was still being investigated.

The attack took place at an upscale restaurant in central Moscow. (Reuters: Anastasia Barashkova)

The woman, the guard and a customer at the Balzi Rossi Italian restaurant were killed instantly in the blast, NAK said.

As of early afternoon on Sunday, local time, there was no further information from Russian authorities, and no one had publicly claimed responsibility.

Footage released by Russian state media showed heavily armed law-enforcement officers, several ambulances and other emergency vehicles at the site.

Ukraine war link speculated

Authorities have not revealed the names of the killed or injured or those of any suspects, but unverified social media reports suggested that a top Russian military commander had been the intended target but had been unharmed.

Drones make life in Russia's cities a 'nightmare' For years, people in Russia's largest and most affluent cities were shielded from the impacts of their country's full-scale invasion of Ukraine, but not anymore.

More than four years into a full-scale war with Ukraine, Russia this year promised better protection for high-ranking military officials after a series of assassinations and attempted killings, which it blamed on Kyiv.

Russian war bloggers, without citing any evidence, were quick to blame Ukraine for the attack. Kyiv did not immediately comment.

The Kommersant Daily suggested that the woman carrying the bomb may not have known about it, and that it had been set off remotely by someone else.

The restaurant's website said the venue had been closed on Saturday for a private event.

AP/Reuters

World.title: Five dead, 41 missing after Indonesian ferry catches fire
World.content:
Five people have been found dead and 41 are missing after an Indonesian ferry with 271 people on board caught fire while at sea.

The captain called the ferry company to report the fire as the vessel sailed from Surabaya in East Java to Makassar in South Sulawesi on Sunday, according to Basarnas, the Indonesian National Search and Rescue Agency.

The captain has not been in contact since.

A total of 225 people on the vessel have been rescued, the regional Surabaya Search and Rescue Agency said.

Video released by Indonesia's National Search and Rescue Agency shows the passenger ferry on fire. (AFP: Basarnas)

Some passengers jumped into the sea and were picked up by a nearby ship.

Four other vessels were on stand-by near the ferry but could not approach because of the risk posed by flammable material on the ferry, Basarnas said.

A larger rescue operation is heading to the site from Surabaya, a six-hour journey from the site of the disaster.

Rescue officers prepare for the search and rescue operation. (Reuters: BASARNAS)

"Based on preliminary reports from the field, passengers are waiting to be evacuated by the vessels in the vicinity of the incident site," said Muhammad Masyhud, a senior official at the Ministry of Transportation.

"The safety of passengers and crew is our top priority. We are continuously coordinating with all relevant parties to ensure that the evacuation process can proceed quickly, safely, and effectively," he said in a statement.

AFP/Reuters

World.title: Candles light up night to honour Melbourne mother Brooke Stephens
World.content:
The family of a Melbourne woman have remembered her as a beautiful, loving mother at a vigil held one week after she was allegedly murdered in her own home.

As the sun set over a park in Clyde North in Melbourne's south-east on Sunday, hundreds of people gathered to pay their respects to local woman Brooke Stephens.

Ms Stephens, 29, died after her partner allegedly attacked her inside their Clyde North home on July 26.

Her partner, 32-year-old Jorden Turney, has been charged with her murder and will face a committal hearing in November.

Friends, families and supporters gathered at Smiths Park Playground to pay tribute to Brooke Stephens. (ABC News: James Oaten)

Memories of Ms Stephens were shared at the vigil, including her love of basketball, which she coached.

Family member Kelly-Ann Faulkner said the majority of the family were still in shock.

"It's really shaken the whole, entire family," she said.

"She has two beautiful little boys that have been devastated by this horrific incident."

Photos and mementos of Brooke Stephens were on display at the vigil. (ABC News: James Oaten)

Ms Faulkner said the two boys had lost their best friend.

"Her sons are in the worst place you could possibly ever think of," she said.

"They won't get to grow up with their mum; they'll go to bed every night wondering where their mum is."

Family members Ellie Stephens (left), Lachlan Timmins and Kelly-Ann Faulkner embraced at the vigil. (ABC News: James Oaten)

Another family member, Lachlan Timmins, fought through tears as he remembered Brooke as a "beautiful, loving sister".

"A good role model to those kids," he said.

Vigil organiser Em Ross said the event was being held to honour Ms Stephen's memory.

"We are here to acknowledge the life she lived, the people who loved her, and the devastating loss being felt by her family, her friends and the wider community," Ms Ross said.

"To Brooke's family and loved ones, we extend our deepest condolences. We cannot begin to understand the weight of your grief, but we hope tonight shows that you are not alone."

Attendees raised their phone lights, adding to candles lit in memory of Brooke Stephens. (ABC News: James Oaten)

As darkness fell across the park, candles were lit and passed around to each attendee, before a minutes silence.

"May each candle represent our collective love, our sorrow and our commitment to creating a safer community," Ms Ross said.

When the 500 candles prepared for the vigil were all taken, people began lighting their mobile phones and shining them into the darkness in support, illuminating the winter night.

Attendees share concerns about domestic violence

Family violence campaigner Sherele Moody from Australian Femicide watch was in attendance at the vigil, and said domestic and family violence was "a continuing epidemic in this country".

Ms Moody called out the state government for perceived inaction on violence against women.

"Victoria has got the highest femicide toll in Australia this year," she said.

Sherele Moody says there has been a surge in public awareness about domestic violence. (ABC News: James Oaten)

Ms Moody said she was being contacted by women in Victoria "every day" who told her they were unable to access support services after experiencing violence.

"We're not even remotely near where we should be to end violence against women and children in this country," she said.

"It's on the state governments to step up and deliver proper fully-funded support services."

World.title: Eight alleged offenders who cut off ankle bracelets spark police manhunt
World.content:
Eight people accused of serious crimes have cut off their ankle bracelets in the past 48 hours, sparking a massive manhunt, WA police have said.

As of 3:30pm on Sunday, the ABC understands six alleged offenders have been caught, leaving two men on the run.

Those people are allegedly serious criminals and are "dangerous to the community", according to Simone Taplin, a representative from WA Police Union.

Sergeant Taplin said six police officers were required to hunt each person, meaning 48 officers were diverted from their usual duties this weekend.

"That's a large amount of resources to look for someone who should be behind bars," she said.

Simone Taplin says a large amount of police resources is diverted to look for alleged offenders. (Supplied)

"Our officers are being called on urgently to go and capture them when they cut their bracelets.

"That stops [police] from attending family and domestic violence, it stops them from attending serious crimes that are occurring."

Still on the run, 40-year-old Jeremy James Miller has pleaded guilty to twice breaching his post-sentence supervision order.

Police say Jeremy James Miller cut off his electronic bracelet in Midland before disappearing. (Supplied: WA Police)

He was deemed by the courts fit to be fitted with a device that police said he cut off in Midland, before disappearing.

Russell Ysandre Damion Dabb, 18, who faces 25 charges, including allegedly breaching bail twice, is the second man on the run.

Russell Dabb is the second man on the run. (Supplied: WA Police)

Police said he took off his device in Mirrabooka at the weekend.

Surge in electronic monitoring

The Department of Justice uses electronic monitoring bracelets, fitted with GPS technology, to track people released on bail or on supervision orders, after they have served a prison sentence.

It is an option available to magistrates and judges when considering if someone should remain behind bars, or if they can be safely released into the community.

But the WA Police Union said it was pushing the management of would-be prisoners onto police, adding there had been a "massive increase in the electronic monitoring of offenders".

Sergeant Taplin says police officers are doing the job of another department. (Supplied)

Sergeant Taplin said people cutting off their monitors has become an "everyday" occurrence.

"[The Department of] Justice aren't managing their criminals effectively, so the police are being asked to do another job for another government department," Sergeant Taplin said.

In a statement, WA Police said "each breach requires an immediate operational response and places additional pressure on police resources, with officers redirected from other policing activities".

Alleged DV offender released without GPS monitoring A man accused of raping and strangling his former partner has been released into the community without a GPS tracking device.

"The cumulative impact of multiple breaches in a short period can be significant, requiring considerable time and resources to investigate and resolve."

The Department of Justice has argued that it did not decide on whether an offender was released into the community or the conditions imposed on an offender, including electronic monitoring.

"Under reforms introduced in 2024, electronic monitoring is mandatory in certain circumstances for family and domestic violence offenders where a court has determined the offender can be safely managed in the community.

"The removal or tampering of an electronic monitoring device is an offence and a breach of supervision conditions.

"When an alleged breach and/or offence is suspected, the Department refers the matter to WA Police for investigation and response to ensure community safety is protected."

Basil Zempilas has criticised the mismanagement in the WA prison system. (ABC News: Courtney Withers)

Opposition Leader Basil Zempilas has blamed the overcrowding in WA jails, saying "these people should be in prison".

"If it was not for the mismanagement of our prison system by this Labor government, those people would not be out of jail with ankle bracelets on that they can cut off, and cause a danger to our community," he told reporters on Sunday.

A report by the state's Inspector of Custodial Services recently found WA prisoners were being subjected to "cruel, inhumane or degrading treatment" because the government has allowed the state's prison system to become "almost functionally broken".

Damning report finds WA prisoners subjected to 'cruel, degrading treatment' WA prisoners are being subjected to "cruel, inhumane or degrading treatment" because the state government has allowed prisons to become "almost fundamentally broken", according to the Inspector of Custodial Services.

A core reason outlined was a 37 per cent increase in the prison population since early 2023.

Premier Roger Cook reiterated his government's "priority [is] to keep the community safe".

"If someone breaks their parole, breaks their bail, if they break any of the conditions, including the ankle bracelets, they will pay the price," he said.

Those in breach can be arrested by police and face jail terms of up to three years and a fine of up to $36,000.

World.title: Record-breaking Premier League move looms for Socceroo
World.content:
Teenage Socceroo Lucas Herrington is on the verge of a move to Premier League club Hull City that would be the most expensive transfer for an Australian player.

Composed central defender Herrington has been the subject of interest from European clubs, including powerhouses like Barcelona and Liverpool, since before the FIFA World Cup.

The 18-year-old's stunning start to life as a Socceroo, and his impressive World Cup debut, has only ramped up interest.

Lucas Herrington currently plays for the Colorado Rapids in the MLS. (Getty Images: MediaNews Group/The Denver Post/Timothy Hurst)

While a deal has not yet been done, MLS club Colorado Rapids are in negotiations with Hull City, with reports of a transfer fee between $35 million and $38 million.

It means the fee for Herrington would smash the $23 million Australian transfer record set by Harry Souttar's move to Leicester City in 2023.

Brisbane Roar product Herrington would also be the only Socceroo in the Premier League this season, at this stage.

Hull City owner Acun Ilicali confirmed the newly-promoted club's interest in Herrington to the BBC on Saturday.

Asked if Herrington was someone Hull were looking at, Ilicali said: "Yes".

"He's [got] very big potential. Very young boy. I think [a] future star," he said.

" We are very close, very close. "

Asked when he thought a decision might be made on Herrington, Ilicali said: "One week".

Herrington, whose contract with the Rapids runs until 2029, with the option of a further year, played a full match on Sunday in a 1-0 win over Austin FC that could be his final game for the club.

ABC Sport Daily podcast ABC Sport Daily is your daily sports conversation. We dive into the biggest story of the day and get you up to speed with everything else that's making headlines.

While the 18-year-old, who suited up for the MLS All-Star team earlier in the week, was made available to local media, it was reported questions about a potential transfer were off limits.

Colorado don't play again until August 16, so it appears likely Sunday's game was Herrington's final bow.

If his move is completed, he will join fellow Socceroos breakout sensations Patrick Beach (Troyes) and Paul Okon-Engstler (FC Koln) in sealing post-World Cup moves to top-five leagues.

Exciting attacker Nestory Irankunda has also been linked to a post-World Cup move away from Watford, but that as yet has not eventuated.

Teen sensation takes Socceroos breakout in his stride Lucas Herrington is on track to become Australia's youngest ever World Cup starter, but the 18-year-old is taking his incredible rise in his stride.

Herrington impressed with his calm and composed displays at the World Cup, playing beyond his years.

The defender stepped up to take a penalty in the shootout against Egypt, but hit the crossbar, as the Socceroos again fell at the first knockout stage.

Brisbane also made headlines during the World Cup after it emerged the club had cashed in early on Herrington when Colorado came knocking to buy out the Roar's sell-on clause on the teenager.

That decision is now set to cost the A-League Men club millions.

AAP

World.title: 'We'll kill you': Sandilands says he received threats in Stefanovic interview
World.content:
Controversial former radio host Kyle Sandilands claims he received death threats after being fired from his KIIS FM breakfast show with co-host Jackie "O" Henderson in February.

In an interview with former Nine Today presenter, Karl Stefanovic, released on YouTube on Sunday, Sandilands said threatening letters had been left at his office.

"There was death threats, letters in my office explaining, 'If you ever do anything on any platform, we'll kill you, we'll hunt you down'," Sandilands said.

" I know these people are lunatics, but what if just one of those lunatics has a weapon? Do you ever think about that? "

Kyle Sandilands was interviewed by Karl Stefanovic for his podcast. (YouTube: The Karl Stefanovic Show)

Sandilands pointed to the fatal shooting of a US health insurance chief executive in New York in 2024 as an example of the escalation of violence towards public figures.

"What is the assassination culture? All these loons feel empowered that they can go and take out a CEO of a health care company in America on the streets of New York," he said.

"We've all got extreme mates … we're probably our mates' extreme mates. But we need to be based in some sort of correct assumption of what life's all about, we can't be having all these extremes."

Since leaving mainstream media in recent months, both broadcasters have moved towards independent podcasting, entertaining a range of figures.

Stefanovic left Nine in June following backlash over his podcast interview with British far-right figure Tommy Robinson.

On his own network, his guest list has increasingly featured figures on the right of Australian politics, including Pauline Hanson, Gerard Rennick and Barnaby Joyce, with much of the conversation focusing on debate about immigration, monoculture and distrust of mainstream news coverage.

'Someone's bad mood'

Much of the conversation between the pair centred on the fallout from the on-air clash that ended the Kyle and Jackie O Show.

During the February 20 argument, Sandilands told Henderson her interest in astrology made her "almost unworkable".

Henderson then told ARN Media, the show's owner, she could no longer work with him and Sandilands was terminated weeks later.

"I was one year into the 10-year plan, and then, due to someone's bad mood, that fell apart," Sandilands said.

Kyle Sandilands reaches settlement Veteran Sydney broadcaster Kyle Sandilands and ARN Media reach a settlement to end a $100 million contract dispute, which had been playing out in the Federal Court.

He added during the 35-minute show that he still did not fully understand what had happened, and would not speak to Henderson until her court case concluded.

He said the sacking itself was not as bad as he imagined.

"People would think, 'He's crushed'. There are people rejoicing and stamping all over the death and the ashes of both of us. But let them. They've got very little joy in their heart, those trolls," he said.

But he said the fallout had taken a heavier toll on staff, including his manager, who he said had been left "projectile vomiting" over the loss of his own job.

Henderson has since launched Federal Court proceedings against ARN, alleging the network failed to act on bullying and psychosocial safety complaints she says she raised about Sandilands's conduct.

Sandilands rejected that he was a bully.

"Women resigned from the radio station to come and work for me," he said.

"That's remarkable for such a horrific bully in the workplace."

Kyle claims he was 'the little person'

Despite his vast wealth, Sandilands said the legal battle in the Federal Court had left him disillusioned with the legal system.

"I've spent hundreds of thousands of dollars with lawyers … only for someone to say, 'It was gross misconduct, you're fired'," he said.

Analysis: Is Stefanovic chasing far right or the algorithm? After more than a quarter of a century on TV, Karl Stefanovic's goodbye didn't go out on free-to-air television, writes Cam Wilson.

"This legal system … it's not fair. Whether I can pay for it or not, it's designed to squash the little person down and in this case, I was a little person."

Stefanovic agreed, saying there was little ordinary people could do if faced with the same circumstances.

"What actually happens to the person in the media, or the person in any corporation, who does just get shown the door and there's no recourse for them? There's absolutely nothing they can do," Stefanovic added.

Sandilands has since launched his own subscription podcast venture, KS Live, and said he had already secured enough funding to operate for three years.

He proposed the notion of joining forces with Stefanovic to form a new corporation, where former radio jockey Ray Hadley could present a midday program.

"There's nothing stopping that," Sandilands said.

World.title: Commonwealth Games 2026 LIVE: Cyclist Georgia Baker to carry flag for closing ceremony; Aussies take silver in final race
World.content:

World.title: House price fall accelerates as rate rises and budget policies hit
World.content:
PoliticsFederalProperty prices House price fall accelerates as rate rises and budget policies hit Shane Wright August 3, 2026 — 12:01am Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Share A A A

The national property market is in its deepest downturn since the Albanese government came to office as interest rates, high cost of living and the May budget’s changes to property taxes combine to wipe thousands of dollars off property values. Figures released by Cotality today show dwelling values in the nation’s capitals dropped by 0.9 per cent through July, led by a steep fall in the value of houses in Sydney and Melbourne. In Sydney, the median house value dropped 1.7 per cent last month to be down 5.9 per cent since the beginning of the year. Despite the fall, the median house value in Sydney remains above $1.5 million. Melbourne’s house values fell by 1.4 per cent in June to be down 3.4 per cent over the past 12 months to $936,528. The city remains the weakest market in the country, with the median dwelling value - which includes houses, units and apartments - now 1.6 per cent down on where it was five years ago.



Both Sydney and Melbourne have been weak since the start of the year, with the fall in values accelerating since the Reserve Bank started lifting interest rates in February. But all major capital city markets are now either slowing or have turned negative. Values dropped in Brisbane (0.6 per cent), Adelaide (0.1 per cent) and Canberra (1 per cent) in June while they improved by just 0.1 per cent in both Perth and Hobart. Related Article Analysis

Property market Saying there’s an upside to falling house prices is sacrilege. But Labor needs to admit it The national median value of a dwelling edged down 0.7 per cent, its largest drop since late 2022, to $928,421. Despite the fall, the national value has only retreated to where it was in March and remains almost $220,000 above its December 2022 level.



Cotality head of research Gerard Burg said a series of demand-side factors were hitting the property market. These included the RBA’s three rate rises, the high prices of every capital city and the May budget’s changes to property taxes, including negative gearing and capital gains tax. He said cost-of-living pressures, including the lift in petrol prices, which climbed sharply through July, were also weighing on potential buyers. Petrol prices are expected to rise again from Monday as the government ends its fuel excise cut. Burg said another factor was supply, as potential sellers held back their properties. Though this would likely put a floor under the entire market, he cautioned home values were likely to continue falling for some time. “Potential vendors are shying away from the market, given the weaker conditions, resulting in a pullback in new listings of properties for sale,” he said. “Combined with the constraints to housing construction, this supply-side response could limit how far home values fall in the current downturn.”



Cotality noted that the biggest falls in value have been among the most expensive properties. Values across the top 20 per cent of the market nationally fell by 3.2 per cent over the past three months. But at the bottom end of the market, dominated by first-time buyers, values increased by 0.3 per cent. Official figures last week showed the largest number of new properties approved for construction in five years, with substantial jumps in NSW, Queensland and Western Australia. While approvals for new homes are running at five-year highs, experts believe that is likely to be shortlived. AMP chief economist Shane Oliver said while more housing stock would come on to the market, it wasn’t enough to maintain downward pressure on property values. He said on a trend basis, around 220,000 homes had been approved over the past 12 months.



“The trouble is that rate hikes, rising costs and project abandonments will likely see it rollover soon and completions continue to run at much lower levels such that the housing shortage will linger longer,” he said. Despite the fall, property values are still well up over the past decade across the country. The smallest increase has been in Melbourne, where values are up by 29.5 per cent, while they have lifted by almost 50 per cent in Sydney. Related Article Analysis

Property prices Sliding housing prices gave the Reserve Bank a surprise helping hand The biggest increases over the past 10 years have been in Brisbane, Perth and Adelaide, where values have more than doubled. The median value of a house remains above $1 million in Sydney, Brisbane ($1.2 million), Adelaide ($1.007 million), Perth ($1.07 million) and Canberra ($1.03 million).



Even over the past year, values in some parts of the country are still growing strongly, including the south-east of Perth (up by 28.2 per cent), the Logan-Beaudesert area of Brisbane (20.8 per cent) and northern parts of Adelaide (13.3 per cent). Auction clearance rates have fallen below 50 per cent for the past two months. Burg said this was partly due to sellers over-estimating what buyers were prepared to pay. “There remains a mismatch between the pricing expectations of buyers and sellers,” he said. World.title: Sliding housing prices gave the Reserve Bank a surprise helping hand
World.content:
Analysis PoliticsFederalProperty prices Sliding housing prices gave the Reserve Bank a surprise helping hand Shane Wright August 3, 2026 — 12:01am Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Share A A A

It’s the helping hand that surprised even the Reserve Bank. The bank always knew that its three rate hikes - in February, March and May - would slow the property market. While governor Michele Bullock will say up hill and down dale that the bank does not target asset prices, the RBA’s interest rate rises were all aimed at taking steam out of the economy. And, as the Reserve Bank knows, climbing house prices make people feel wealthier and happier, leaving them more likely to open their digital wallets. Michele Bullock will take any assistance she can get to help cool inflation. Louie Douvis The so-called wealth effect also works in reverse. Falling property prices are more likely than not to make consumers a little wary when it comes to spending a dollar, adding to any deflationary pressures in the economy.



Property prices, particularly those in Sydney where residents don’t get out of bed unless they’ve got a $900,000 mortgage strapped to their back, were already responding to the RBA’s rate hikes through March and April. But it is clear that the May budget, and Treasurer Jim Chalmers’ array of changes to negative gearing and capital gains tax, is amplifying those higher interest rates. Related Article Exclusive

Property market High-priced homes have broken the intergenerational bargain This wasn’t on the Reserve’s radar when it started jacking up interest rates in February. While the government was considering a range of tax changes, it was a long way off from a settled position. And even that was upended by the events of February 28 when the US and Israel began their war against Iran. Economists often bemoan that the RBA and the government of the day are often in conflict. There were plenty upset that the May budget contained a forecast deficit of $31.5 billion, larger than the just completed financial year.



Yet, it is apparent – especially if you spend your time tracking the social media posts of real estate agents – that the government’s tax changes have contributed to the nationwide slowdown in prices and auction activity. If people aren’t buying and selling homes, their demand for everything from real estate agents to removalists to new furniture also falls. Last week’s better-than-expected inflation figures revealed some deep falls in prices for goods associated with the housing sector. Furniture prices in Sydney, for instance, fell by 4.6 per cent. Household textiles fell by 2.1 per cent. Household appliances were cheaper, both for large ones (minus 1.9 per cent) and small (minus 0.7 per cent). Even glassware and tableware prices tumbled by 5.5 per cent. Some of those falls are likely due to the stronger Australian dollar which pushes down the price of imported goods. But a slowing property market means people are less likely to want or need new furniture or plates or refrigerators. It also puts pressure on lenders to offer better deals – aka, cheaper prices or improved services – to win customers from a diminishing pool.



Chalmers and the rest of the government will never admit that their policies were aimed at cutting property prices. And the Reserve Bank is loath to concede that a drop in house values is a positive in its ongoing fight against inflation. Not that we have hit an affordability nirvana quite yet. Sydney’s median house value is still above $1.5 million. Also in the $1 million club are Brisbane, Adelaide, Perth and Canberra. Melbourne is not part of the $1 million club - something for which prospective home buyers should be glad. Even the drop in values revealed by Cotality today takes the national dwelling value back to where it was in March. So, we’re not quite back to the 50 per cent price crash of the 1890s. But the interaction of tighter monetary policy and fewer tax incentives for investors in the property market is clearly helping in the battle to get inflation down. World.title: Big carrot, more stick under news bargaining plan
World.content:
PoliticsFederalNews Bargaining Incentive Big carrot, more stick under news bargaining plan Shane Wright August 3, 2026 — 12:01am Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Share A A A

Global tech giants have sandbagged their wider revenue streams but face losing a larger share of their advertising income under the federal government’s plan to force them into funding Australian journalism. The final details of the government’s News Bargaining Incentive, which it hopes to bring to parliament within weeks, show a key concession to companies including Meta, Google and TikTok in a bid to encourage them to strike commercial deals with Australian news publishers. Big tech companies face paying for Australian news on their sites under a plan to protect local companies. Getty But the concession has come with a caveat aimed at ensuring local publishers share in the revenue that tech giants are accused of generating by effectively siphoning Australian-produced news onto their own sites without paying. Under the original incentive plan, digital search and tech platform companies with revenues of at least $250 million a year would face a 2.25 per cent charge against their total revenues if they failed to come to a commercial deal with four local news producers. Companies can offset the charge by signing tax-deductible deals worth about 1.5 per cent of revenue.



The policy is aimed at ensuring news outlets share in some of the income generated by their work that is often spread, without charge, on the tech giants’ various platforms. The money is expected to flow back to the employment of journalists. Related Article AI Microsoft agrees to pay Nine for journalism in major AI deal Tech companies argued the charge on total revenue was unfair as parts of their operations had nothing to do with news. The new incentive plan, to be released on Monday, has reduced the scope of revenue to only that made by the tech companies’ digital advertising streams. But to ensure the same amount of revenue is raised by incentive, the rate will be increased from 2.25 per cent to 2.5 per cent. Tech companies will have to strike deals with at least six publishers.



The rate for voluntary deals has not changed. The original proposal excluded sites such as LinkedIn, which have claimed they do not carry news. But LinkedIn and other “professional networking services” will now face the charge. Treasury estimates the policy will deliver between $200 million and $250 million a year to local media. Assistant Treasurer Daniel Mulino said the government believed financially sustainable journalism was vital to a well-functioning democracy. “While we are making some changes to the News Bargaining Incentive, they do not alter the intent of the legislation and remain true to the policy rationale,” he said.



“We want digital platforms to do deals with a diverse range of media organisations and have shown good faith with both the platforms and media companies during the consultation process.” When the original plan was unveiled, it attracted strident criticism from Meta, which described it as a “discriminatory, retroactive tax” that was poorly designed and “grossly unfair”. But the incentive has broad support in the Australian news sector, which has faced sharp falls in revenue and been forced into substantial job losses over several years. Apart from the incentive itself, the government has finalised the details of the News Journalism Payment Scheme that will be funded by the charge. The definition of journalists will be broadened to include “more essential news roles” and freelancers, there will be larger revenue flows for regional-based publishers or those that service particular communities, while a grants program will be created specifically for publishers and start-ups with revenues under $150,000 a year.



Communications Minister Anika Wells said the increase in support for smaller and regional publishers recognised the challenges they faced and their importance to their local communities. Start the day with a summary of the day’s most important and interesting stories, analysis and insights.
